rows.episode_title: Treetop Treats / Eva the Ghost Catcher
rows.synopsis: Eva enters the Treetop Treat Contest to win a Golden Apron for her teacher.
rows.situation: Eva spots the one thing Ms. Featherbottom is missing, an art smock, and decides to win her the Golden Apron from the Treetop Treat Contest. Then the most talented artist in class, Sue Clawson, enters the same contest with a three-scoop masterpiece, and Eva's first attempt, everything-nachos, comes out a gloopy disaster.
rows.coping: Acorn carrot muffins rescue the round one, and the collision with Sue's ice cream ends the rivalry instead of the contest: both were entering for Ms. Featherbottom. Combined into one entry, muffins plus pecan butter ice cream plus sprinkles, they win, and the single Golden Apron goes exactly where Eva first pictured it, on her teacher.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: baking and contest romp plays 2-4; the competing-for-the-same-person reframe and the we-both-wanted-to-give-it beat land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis already centers the contest and the teacher gift; the script adds the Sue rivalry, the everything-nachos failure, and the collision-to-teamwork turn.
rows.per_story_synopsis: When Eva notices her teacher could use an art smock, she enters the Treetop Treat Contest to win the Golden Apron for her, then discovers her toughest competition is Sue Clawson, who is great at everything. Everything-nachos fail, acorn carrot muffins rise, and one collision later the two rivals realize they were baking for the very same teacher. One combined treat and one shared victory later, the Golden Apron lands where it belongs, and Eva's diary gets the best kind of ending, the kind you bake together.

rows.episode_title: Treetop Treats / Eva the Ghost Catcher
rows.synopsis: Eva and her friends hunt a ghost that is haunting their fun nest.
rows.situation: A white blur keeps flashing through Treetopington's best spots, the fun nest, the birdbath, the snack stand, and Eva is certain it is a ghost. Jacob keeps saying he does not think it is one, and Eva is so sure she is right that she does not stop to listen.
rows.coping: The ghost map turns out to be a friend map: the blur follows the welcome map Eva's mom made, and it is Kiera, the new neighbor, exploring town at full speed. Eva apologizes to Jacob for not listening, announces town-wide that there is no ghost, and opens the flaptastic fun nest with the fastest new friend in Treetopington.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: ghost-hunt chase comedy plays 2-4; the confident-mistake arc, not listening to the friend who was right, and the new-neighbor payoff land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis names the hunt; the script supplies the map clue, the Jacob-was-right admission, and the public no-ghost announcement.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Something fast, white, and undeniably spooky is flashing all over Treetopington, and the flaptastic fun nest cannot open with a ghost on the loose. Eva becomes a ghost catcher, Jacob becomes the friend nobody listens to, and the chase barrels through birdbaths, snack stands, and the world's largest pine cone. The trail, it turns out, is a welcome map, and the ghost is Kiera, the new neighbor, seeing the town Eva loves at a speed worth apologizing for. The fun nest opens, the flag goes up, and the town gains both an answer and a friend.

rows.synopsis: Eva tries to help put Baby Mo to bed.
rows.situation: Eva hears her parents call Humphrey a great helper and wants the same warm blanket around her heart, so she appoints herself co-babysitter for Baby Mo's big night. Her super helpful list, flapping jacks, rocking nests, lullabies, even pretending to be asleep, only makes the wide-awake baby more awake, and the sun is coming up with her promise broken.
rows.coping: Out of list, Eva has to watch Humphrey's quiet answer work: Baby Mo just needed to be held by his big brother. At sunrise she gives the credit away honestly, telling their parents it was all Humphrey, then declares her list super unhelpful in her diary without a hint of bitterness. The dream team gets its feather ruffle shuffle after all.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: wide-awake-baby comedy plays 2-4; the helper-credit arc, doing less to earn more, and Eva's genuine praise for Humphrey land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'tries to help' is the frame; the script supplies the escalating list, the list running out, and Eva handing Humphrey the credit she wanted for herself.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Eva wants what Humphrey has, the words great helper, so she joins his babysitting shift armed with a numbered list of sleep tricks. Every trick makes Baby Mo more awake: flapping jacks, rocking nests, a lullaby with guitar, even owlets pretending to sleep, which only invites a baby to wake them. As the sun rises on a broken promise, the answer turns out to be the one thing that was never on the list, and Eva finds that saying her brother figured it out feels warmer than she expected.

rows.synopsis: Ms. Featherbottom invites Eva and Lucy to play a special role in her wedding.
rows.situation: Eva and Lucy are picked as flower owlets and go all in on razzle-dazzle: armloads of petals, feather crowns, a wow walk choreographed by Baby Mo himself. Then the wind takes every single petal right as the guests arrive, and being flower owlets with no flowers is just being owlets.
rows.coping: Looking at the bride and groom resets the whole plan: they are the stars, not us. The crowns they made for themselves go on Ms. Featherbottom and Mr. Swoopington instead, the walk is a plain skip-flap-scatter with the last few petals, and the diary lands it: tonight was not about the razzle-dazzle, it was about being part of their night.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: petal-scattering and wow-walk comedy plays 2-4; the spotlight-reframe and the give-the-crown-away turn land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a special role' hides the showmanship escalation, the wind disaster, and the bride-and-groom-first resolution. vibe provisional: drafted as warm, mapped to the guide's calm/silly/energetic vocabulary (vibe rule undecided).
rows.per_story_synopsis: Being asked to be flower owlets at Ms. Featherbottom's wedding calls for maximum razzle-dazzle, and Eva and Lucy deliver: bundles of petals, self-made crowns, and a wow walk borrowed from a baby brother's waddle. Then the wind empties their baskets in front of the arriving guests. The recovery is not a replacement plan but a perspective shift, because the wedding was never their show. The crowns go where the wow belongs, on the bride and groom, and two owlets discover that scattering the last few petals for someone you love is the whole job.

rows.synopsis: A story time character inspires Eva to plan a secret project.
rows.situation: Eva is honored to carry the class acorn, just like the littlest owlet in the founding story of Treetopington, and decides one acorn is not enough: she will secretly plant a whole forest. But acorns are hard to plant alone, and the surprise is discovered mid-dig, ruined before it is revealed.
rows.coping: Ms. Featherbottom releases the surprise gracefully: it does not matter whether it is a surprise. The whole class joins the forest planting, Eva's diary reframes the day, she thought she should do it alone like the littlest owlet, but it is more special to do it together, and someday owls from far and wide will rest on what they planted.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: digging and acorn comedy plays 2-4; the secret-project-backfire, being seen before ready, and the alone-versus-together lesson land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'plan a secret project' names the setup; the script adds the acorn-carrier honor, the forest upgrade, and the caught-mid-dig turn that reframes the surprise. retagged: 'excited, embarrassed' to 'happy, embarrassed' per the ratified 18-term vocabulary (off-list terms removed). vibe provisional: drafted as warm, mapped to the guide's calm/silly/energetic vocabulary (vibe rule undecided).
rows.per_story_synopsis: When the class learns their big oak tree grew from one little owlet's planted acorn, Eva gets the honor of planting the next one. She quietly decides to top the story: a whole secret forest, planted solo, revealed to gasps. Digging alone is harder than stories let on, and getting caught kneeling in the dirt deflates the big reveal entirely. What she gets instead is better than gasps, an entire class grabbing acorns, and a first lesson in the difference between a surprise and a gift you build together.

rows.synopsis: Humphrey's talent comes in handy during a Treetopington event.
rows.situation: Eva invents the Treetop Swap so nobody has to throw away what someone else needs, and Humphrey keeps offering his organizing system. Every offer lands the same way: it is her idea, and she wants to do it her way, right up until the swap pile becomes a messy mountain and she cannot remember who wanted the owlball.
rows.coping: Humphrey wins her over the moment she asks, and his reassurance does the identity repair: it is still your idea no matter how you do it. Rows for seeing, lists for haves and wants, purple boots on the want-it list, and the swap turns into the ginormous success Eva wanted, finished with a puzzle they solve together, edges first.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: swap-chaos comedy plays 2-4; the my-idea pride, the overwhelmed turn, and the help-does-not-take-ownership lesson land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'Humphrey's talent comes in handy' is the outcome; the script's spine is Eva refusing help three times, the mountain of stuff, and the it-is-still-your-idea reassurance. vibe provisional: drafted as warm, mapped to the guide's calm/silly/energetic vocabulary (vibe rule undecided).
rows.per_story_synopsis: Eva's new event, the Treetop Swap, runs on one rule: old to you, new to someone else. It also runs directly into Humphrey's offers of a system, which Eva declines with growing firmness, because the swap is her idea and her way is working exactly how she wants it. The pile disagrees. Buried in a mountain nobody can see into, with requests slipping through her memory, Eva asks for the system herself and hears the sentence every kid with a big idea needs: it is still your idea, no matter how you do it.

rows.synopsis: Kiera adopts an adorable hedgehog and leans on Eva for caretaking advice.
rows.situation: Kiera's first pet, a hedgehog named Jelly, makes Eva a teacher: Pet School opens with lessons on feeding, playing, and tricks. But Baxter discovers wing snacks on his own, Jelly and Kiera invent their own games, and the pets keep choosing Kiera's way, until Eva quietly decides the student has outgrown the teacher and nearly goes home.
rows.coping: Baxter follows Eva away from the fun and answers the wobble without a word: he still chooses his person. Kiera hands the identity back too, best teacher ever, because Eva taught her the part that matters most, loving your pet. They graduate to lesson four and to a school where both of them teach.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: pet-school comedy plays 2-4; the outgrown-teacher wobble, the should-I-just-go-home beat, and the both-of-us-teach resolution land 5-7. vocabulary gap: the beat is closest to jealousy or feeling inadequate, neither on the approved 16-term list, so tagged disappointed/proud as nearest. script_vs_synopsis: 'leans on Eva for caretaking advice' omits the student-surpasses-teacher turn and Eva's near-exit. vibe provisional: drafted as warm, mapped to the guide's calm/silly/energetic vocabulary (vibe rule undecided).
rows.per_story_synopsis: A new hedgehog named Jelly turns Eva into the founder of Pet School, with a curriculum built from life with Baxter. Then class starts teaching itself: Baxter invents wing snacks, Kiera and Jelly out-bounce and out-fetch the demonstrations, and Eva is left wondering why anyone needs her, and nearly leaving before anyone says so. The answer arrives on quiet wings, a best friend who followed her out of the fun, and a student who says the loving-pet part was always hers to give. Pet School ends the night with two teachers.

rows.synopsis: Eva and her mom embark on a photography journey.
rows.situation: Dad carves a picture frame, and Eva wants to fill it with a photo as good as Mom's famous flower shot. The garden's moonflower is the perfect subject, but it opens only in moonlight, for a few moments, and when the moment finally comes, the picture is missed by a beak.
rows.coping: Mom does not fix it, she just keeps the camera out, and the night fills up with practice shots, silly faces, a pine-cone race, and memories saved to the diary. Looking back at them changes the ask: Dad's frame gets a photo of his favorite photographers having fun, and Eva decides memories beat a million-zillion flower photos.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: blurry-practice and silly-face comedy plays 2-4; the missed-once-chance disappointment and the memories-are-the-picture lesson land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'a photography journey' undersells the moonflower's only-opens-in-moonlight stakes, the exact missed moment, and the frame-filling resolution.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Dad's handmade frame needs one flaptastic photo, and Eva knows which one: a flower like Mom's, ideally the garden's legendary moonflower, which opens for a few moonlit moments only. A mother-daughter adventure of practice shots, cloud-watching, and statue-still waiting follows, and the flower opens exactly on schedule, for everyone but the camera. The ride home is quiet until the diary comes out, and the pictures they forgot they were taking turn out to be the ones Dad wants framed.

rows.episode_title: Nest Buddies / Game Night Under the Stars
rows.synopsis: On a Hoot Troop trip, Eva works hard to impress Sue.
rows.situation: Eva draws Sue as her nest buddy for her first night away from home and sees her opening: be the best nest buddy ever. But Sue is so Sue about it, already-built nest, snacks for the whole troop, honey-glazed pecans, and Eva's one sticky pine cone cannot compete, sap-stuck wings and all.
rows.coping: The one-upping stops when the truth does: Eva says it plainly, you are the best nest buddy ever, and Sue's answer dismantles the contest, she made her twig chairs from the twigs Eva carried and was just about to eat that pine cone. Neither one has to be the best, and with the worry gone Eva finally enjoys the trip and the sunrise.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: nest-building and sap-stuck comedy plays 2-4; the comparison spiral (I will never be a better nest buddy than Sue) and the compete-versus-enjoy reframe land 5-7. vocabulary gap: the felt emotion is closest to envy or feeling not-good-enough, neither on the approved 16-term list, so tagged disappointed/frustrated as nearest. script_vs_synopsis: 'works hard to impress Sue' is the engine; the script adds the repeated being-outdone beats and the mutual-credit turn. vibe provisional: drafted as warm, mapped to the guide's calm/silly/energetic vocabulary (vibe rule undecided).
rows.per_story_synopsis: Eva's first overnight trip comes with a Hoot Troop tradition, a nest buddy to take care of, and Eva plans to be the best one in troop history. Her nest buddy is Sue, who is best at everything, navigation, sunscreen, snack spectaculars, and every Eva effort lands one step behind. A sap-glued pine cone and two stuck wings slow the race down just enough for the truth to come out, and it turns out Sue has been using Eva's twigs, eating Eva's pine cone, and feeling out-nest-buddied herself. Nobody has to be the best, and the sunrise is better that way.

rows.episode_title: Nest Buddies / Game Night Under the Stars
rows.synopsis: The owlets compete in a series of games and team up to solve a sudden problem.
rows.situation: Game night has owlball at the end of it, and Eva hurries through every game before it like the pace is the point. Slow, careful Jacob stretches, waits, retrieves a special new owlball, then flaps it into a sap-covered branch, and Eva's rush-to-fix ideas, pulling, kicking, make it worse.
rows.coping: The turnaround is Eva handing the clock back: take as much time as you need to think. Jacob's answer uses the sap itself, a vine stuck to the ball, tugged like tug-the-vine, and it works. Her diary lands the lesson in her own voice: Jacob does not move at my speed, and that is a good thing. The night ends with a brand-new game, vineball.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: game-night romp plays 2-4; the hurrying-versus-thinking arcs and the protect-his-time-to-think beat land 5-7. retagged under the ratified 18-term vocabulary (impatience added 2026-11-11); impatience was previously flagged as an off-list gap. script_vs_synopsis: 'team up to solve a sudden problem' hides that the rush itself caused the problem and that slowing down was the fix. retagged: 'impatient, excited' to 'impatient, happy' per the ratified 18-term vocabulary (off-list terms removed).
rows.per_story_synopsis: Game night under the stars ends with owlball, the best game there is, so Eva sprints through tug-the-vine and acorn roll to get there faster. The pace falls apart around Jacob, who stretches, double-checks for sap, and finally gets his new special owlball stuck exactly where he feared. Every quick fix wedges it deeper, and the game only resumes when Eva gives the slowest owlet in Treetopington the one thing she never gives anyone, time. His sap-and-vine rescue works, the diary gets a new entry about good things that take a while, and vineball is born.

rows.episode_title: Eva's Big Catch / Carlos's Juice Stand
rows.synopsis: Grandma leads Humphrey and Eva on a mushroom-catching mission.
rows.situation: Eva is finally old enough for the mushroom-catching trip with Grandma, training pole and all, and arrives carrying the photo of Humphrey's famous Big One from last year. Humphrey catches another big one while Eva's pole snags, her heavy prize turns out to be a rock, and her only catch is the smallest mushroom anyone has ever seen. The diary wobble is bare: Humphrey will always be Grandma's favorite.
rows.coping: Grandma melts the comparison whole: it does not matter if you catch big mushrooms, small mushrooms, or none at all, and no, there is no favorite grandowlet, she loves them both this much (wings wide). The tiny mushroom becomes a necklace she will always wear to remember this special time with her grandowlet Eva, and the photo says teeny tiny mushroom.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: rock-catch and chant comedy plays 2-4; the favorite-grandchild worry and the no-favorites, wings-wide reassurance land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'mushroom-catching mission' is the frame; the script adds the training pole, the Big One photo, the rock catch, and the necklace resolution. vibe provisional: drafted as warm, mapped to the guide's calm/silly/energetic vocabulary (vibe rule undecided).
rows.per_story_synopsis: Eva's first mushroom-catching trip with Grandma comes with a training pole, a famous sibling trophy to live down, and a heart full of one question: is Humphrey the favorite? While Humphrey lands another Big One, Eva snags a branch, catches a rock, and finally nets a mushroom so small it needs a second look. Then Grandma says the thing that fixes the whole day, there is no favorite, the love comes in equal amounts, and the smallest mushroom in the forest becomes a necklace built for exactly one grandowlet.

rows.episode_title: Eva's Big Catch / Carlos's Juice Stand
rows.synopsis: Eva shakes things up at the local juice stand.
rows.situation: Carlos needs someone to run his beloved juice stand for one night, and Eva volunteers with an upgrade in mind: more kinds of juice than his one blueberry. To fit them all in, she skips his steps one by one, the tasting, the full press, the pine sap, until the stand is serving cran-pepper-anchovy delight and the customers are gone.
rows.coping: Carlos comes back from his grandma's and diagnoses it kindly: all the steps are important, and they took him a long time, and a lot of blech, to figure out. One new juice, made together with every step kept, becomes Happy Sappy Peachberry Juice, the customers return, and Eva's diary credits the whole thing to doing all of the steps.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: wild-flavor comedy plays 2-4; the shortcut-costs-customers arc and the steps-were-earned lesson land 5-7. emotion drawn from the ratified 18-term list (impatience added 2026-11-11). script_vs_synopsis: 'shakes things up' names the experiment; the script supplies the step-skipping cascade, the empty-stand low, and Carlos's blech backstory.
rows.per_story_synopsis: One night behind Carlos's juice stand is not enough time for Eva to serve his way, so she speeds up: more flavors, fewer steps, no tasting, a little less pressing, who needs the pine sap anyway. The customers get surprises like cherry-pepper and blueberry onion, and they vote with their wings. Carlos returns from his grandmother's to an empty stand and a confession, and instead of scolding, he shares how long his steps took to earn, then invites one new juice, made properly, together. Happy Sappy Peachberry Juice brings everybody back.

rows.situation: Eva's first sleepover runs on a list of super-duper plans, and the plans fail in order: no clouds for cloud-watching, paper too wet to paint, and Baby Mo finds the treasure-hunt pine cone before the hunt begins. While Eva scrambles to the next idea, her guests are playing, and she almost misses a whole sleepover of fun happening without her.
rows.coping: The reveal arrives in the guests' own voices: daytime leaf-jumping is super-duper, and this is the most fun sleepover ever. Eva's diary does the honest math, it did not matter that her plans were not super or duper, because her friends know how to have fun and do not need her to make it for them. She joins the game she was busy managing, and the late-arriving clouds get written into a cloudy story.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: plan-flop comedy plays 2-4; the hosting anxiety, the missed-fun reveal, and the friends-are-already-fun lesson land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'hosts her first sleepover' hides the plan-by-plan collapse, the literal it's-hopeless low, and the fun-was-happening-without-me turn.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Eva has planned her first sleepover down to the leaf piles, and the universe declines to cooperate: cloudless skies, wet watercolors, and a baby brother who wins the treasure hunt solo. Convinced the whole night is a disaster, Eva keeps rushing to the next plan while her guests laugh without her. The rescue is not a plan at all, it is the discovery that the sleepover has been fun the entire time, and the hostess finally jumps into the leaf pile she was too busy to notice.

rows.synopsis: Lucy's art making keeps getting interrupted by Eva asking her to help other owlets.
rows.situation: Lantern day at school should be Lucy's showcase, but her blackberry-paint idea sends Eva recruiting her for Carlos, Sue, Jacob, and Kiera, one classmate at a time, without ever asking Lucy first. Eva's own sky lantern stays blank until Lucy, out of time for her Springtime Wonder-lantern, finally says she cannot help right now, and Eva cannot understand why.
rows.coping: Lucy explains it plainly: she spent all her time on everyone else's lanterns and now has none for her own. Eva owns the pattern, I should have asked you before I said yes for you, hands over her own petals, and solves her stars herself with a twig and a what-would-Lucy-do. Lucy gets the switch, the thanks, and the choice next time, because helping is hers to give.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: lantern-decorating plays 2-4; the volunteering-someone-else's-time arc, the apology, and the helping-is-her-choice lesson land 5-7. vocabulary gap: Eva's dominant felt state after the no is guilt, which is not on the 18-term list, so tagged confused/embarrassed as nearest. script_vs_synopsis: the synopsis states the interruption pattern; the script adds the blank-lantern cost, the first-no moment, and Eva's self-reliance turn.
rows.per_story_synopsis: Ms. Featherbottom's lantern project turns the class into artists, and Lucy into the most in-demand idea bank in Treetopington, because Eva keeps offering her services to whoever needs one. By the time the lanterns are due, everyone else's glows and the Springtime Wonder-lantern is bare, and the friend who says no for the first time is the one being told she is not helping. Eva repairs it the Lucy way: return the petals, poke her own stars with a twig, and hand the honor of lighting the class tree to the owlet who lit everyone else's.

rows.synopsis: Anxiously awaiting pinecone pizza night, Eva helps her dad work faster.
rows.situation: Dad's new Pine Forest route means later nights, and the first casualty is pinecone pizza night. Eva wakes him before sunrise to speed the route, hurries him past snack breaks, dumps a whole bag of mail, and still loses the race with sunset, hearing her dad apologize for being too late.
rows.coping: Sorting the scattered mail shows Eva what the route actually carries, a pan flute from a sister, a hatchday present, a postcard from grandowlets, in other words, presents, music, and happiness. The plan flips from getting Dad home to giving back: while he finishes, the family builds a lumpy, peppery pinecone pizza thingy, and Dad declares it better than his because everybody made it.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: dropped-mail and lumpy-pizza comedy plays 2-4; the what-does-Dad's-work-mean realization and the role-reversal dinner land 5-7. script_vs_synopsis: 'helps her dad work faster' is the engine; the script adds the mail catastrophe, the happiness discovery, and the family-cooks-for-Dad reversal. retagged: 'disappointed, kind' to 'disappointed, proud' per the ratified 18-term vocabulary (off-list terms removed). vibe provisional: drafted as warm, mapped to the guide's calm/silly/energetic vocabulary (vibe rule undecided).
rows.per_story_synopsis: Pinecone pizza night is sacred, and Dad's longer mail route is threatening it, so Eva becomes his delivery partner, sunrise wake-up and all. The speed run scatters mail across the forest and the pizza across the evening, and somewhere in the pickup Eva reads what she has been delivering, music, presents, and happiness for owls who need it. Dad flies home to a pizza made by the family he feeds all day, lumpy with too much pepper, and better than his, he says, for exactly that reason.

rows.synopsis: Eva winds up on the front page of the town newspaper.
rows.situation: One seed-catching save puts Eva on the front page of the Treetopington Times, and one headline stops feeling like enough. She chases the next story, owlball over the world's largest pine cone, acorn stacking, both crash, and then she hands the paper a better story, Sue and Carlos's brand-new pumpkin seed bread, and feels the small honest ache: I wish the story was about me.
rows.coping: Watching her shared story work, the whole town baking the recipe, teaches the reframe: what goes in the paper are stories that make owls' lives better, not stories about being seen. The ache gets said out loud to Mom, and it gets outgrown in the same scene as Eva recommends Lucy's dance for the next front page.
rows.notes: vibe provisional (felt-energy draft; brand-vs-felt rule undecided). mixed age: acorn-stacking and headline comedy plays 2-4; the enough-vs-more arc, the named envy, and the share-the-story turn land 5-7. vocabulary gap: the confession is closest to envy, not on the 18-term list, so tagged disappointed/excited as nearest. script_vs_synopsis: 'winds up on the front page' undersells the second-fame chase, the two failed stunts, and the generosity resolution. retagged: 'disappointed, excited' to 'disappointed, proud' per the ratified 18-term vocabulary (off-list terms removed).
rows.per_story_synopsis: Eva saves a jar of seeds and lands on the front page, and suddenly one headline feels like a habit to keep. The stunts get bigger and the landings get harder, and the newsstand stays Eva-less. Then a whiff of pumpkin seed bread shows her the better story, one that makes the whole town's life tastier, and she gives it to the paper herself. The front page belongs to Sue and Carlos this time, and the owlet who shared it discovers the part that never gets old, reading about friends.

rows.synopsis: As Treetopington celebrates a special holiday, Eva helps a lost oriole look for his family, and learns the true meaning of community.
rows.situation: During a special Treetopington holiday, Eva finds an oriole who is lost and far from his family, and she takes on the search while the whole town celebrates around them.
rows.coping: The synopsis points to the resolution shape: Eva helps the lost oriole look for his family, and the search becomes a lesson in what community means, a town showing up for one lost bird. Specific beats and the exact resolution are not verifiable this pass.
